migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Language Quality findings were independently re-adjudicated against the current fixed five-component design rubric. Legacy normalized scores were retained only for audit and were not used to derive component levels. The snapshot is bound to exact source evidence and the current validator recomputes scores.

recertifier.provider_model_provenance_claim: No Anthropic/Sonnet call is claimed for these reconstructed judgments.

component_findings.abstraction_ceremony: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Reusable abstractions such as types, interfaces/traits/generics or equivalent mechanisms can be declared and consumed without excessive scaffolding. Evidence basis: Manual inspection of template/programs/java/micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial samples. Java requires explicit type declarations, boilerplate class wrapper, explicit access modifiers, manual loop indices, and verbose System.out.printf/Locale ceremony for numeric formatting compared to more concise languages. Java 16+ records (used in mb04, mb09 for multi-value Result types) reduce boilerplate versus classic POJOs, and var type-inference plus enhanced for-loops help conciseness in idiomatic modern Java, but mandatory class enclosure and lack of top-level functions keep token counts higher than more concise peers for equivalent algorithmic content. | mb04.java (~72 lines) implements a 4-accumulator floating point workload; a terser language typically needs fewer structural lines due to no mandatory class wrapper and less explicit typing. | mb09.java repeats explicit double[] declarations and manual loops for mean/variance/correlation/histogram computation; idiomatic Java stays close to raw loop form since vectorized library shortcuts would violate fairness rules, but explicit typing and required class/method scaffolding add overhead relative to inferred-type languages. | Adversarial programs (ADV series) show standard Java ceremony (explicit class declaration, main(String[] args) signature, exception handling boilerplate) required on every entry point. | 0-100, 100 = maximally con…

metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic mandatory ceremony for the same kinds of ordinary programs. Do not reuse raw LOC/bytes/tokens as the score and do not reward external libraries.

component_findings.consistency_regular_forms: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Similar concepts use regular forms with few special-case spellings or context-dependent surface rules. Evidence basis: Manual inspection of the same micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial program corpus for naming clarity, structural organization, comment density, and cognitive load of idiomatic Java constructs. | Consistent naming conventions (Lcg, Result, workload()) and doc-style comments in mb04/mb09 make algorithmic intent clear; explicit static typing on every field/variable aids readability by making data flow and units unambiguous. | record types (Result(double s1, double s2, double s3, double s4)) communicate immutable multi-value returns compactly and readably, superior to raw tuples or untyped maps. | Explicit block braces, consistent 4-space indentation, and one-statement-per-line style keep nested loops (mb09 moment/correlation/histogram passes) easy to follow despite algorithmic density. | Minor readability costs: verbose exception/generic boilerplate and required System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, ...) ceremony for locale-safe numeric formatting, more explicit than higher-level languages but not harmful to comprehension. | 0-100, 100 = maximally readable for an experienced engineer with no external context. Java scored 83: strong static typing and naming conventions aid comprehension; verbosity slightly increases visual scanning cost but does not obscure algorithmic intent.
